clue.text: Has news of English vehicle

parts.note: someone who has news of something hears about it

explanation.surface: A report about some English car or bus, as if from a motoring bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: A funeral car carrying the coffin is a particular kind of vehicle.

clue.text: British want to include 'ER', a TV series

parts.note: to want something is to lack it
to include something is to add it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A British production seems to want ER, the hospital drama, folded into its schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACKADDER is the BBC historical comedy starring Rowan Atkinson; 'ER' looks like the American hospital show but just supplies its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC sitcom with Rowan Atkinson ran as four series of television comedy.

clue.text: Very very indifferent

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
again so means very

explanation.surface: Someone describes a thing as extremely, extremely mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifferent here means mediocre, neither good nor bad, which is the sense of the hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Precise remedy

definitions.meaning: an old medical sense: a drug that cures one particular disease

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes an exact cure for a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and clearly defined is the common adjective sense; as a noun it is a medicine for one disease.

clue.text: Choral music singers delight staff

parts.note: glee is delight or joy
a club is a heavy stick or staff

explanation.surface: Members of a choir please the employees of the place they perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as employees but is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A singing society performing part-songs is a group of choral singers.

clue.text: The Parisian soon ringing editor put under pressure

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: ringing means the word for soon surrounds the word for editor

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A Frenchman will soon be telephoning an editor to put pressure on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is an idiom for pressuring or intimidating them.

clue.text: Investor receiving money, as one exchanging favours for mutual advantage

definitions.text: one exchanging favours for mutual advantage

indicators.note: receiving means the investor word takes the money word inside it

parts.note: a backer is someone who invests in a venture
scratch is slang for money

explanation.surface: A financier pockets cash in return for doing favours.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, someone who trades favours (you scratch my back, I'll scratch yours) is described this way.

clue.text: Disapprove of old unpredictable popes

indicators.note: unpredictable means the letters of popes behave erratically and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone objects to past popes who acted erratically.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to disapprove of it; the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Troublesome situation weak characters raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: wets is British slang for feeble, ineffectual people

explanation.surface: A tricky situation arises when feeble people are promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a 'wet' is a feeble person, notably a moderate Tory in the Thatcher years.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being in a worried or difficult state.

clue.text: Marvellous, very amusing detailed material

parts.note: fab is short for fabulous, marvellous

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed: the word for very amusing loses its last letter

parts.note: rich can mean highly amusing or ironic, as in that's rich

explanation.surface: Someone praises a cloth as wonderful, witty and intricately made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like intricate but means having the tail cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or textile is the everyday sense of material here.

clue.text: Mostly bad-tempered note

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: crotchety means irritable or grumpy

explanation.surface: A cross message, written by a grumpy person.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a quarter-note is a note value, one beat in common time.

clue.text: Widespread stick for military advisers

parts.note: general means widespread, as in general opinion
a staff is a long stick

explanation.surface: A commonly used walking stick is issued to military consultants.
explanation.definitionFit: The officers who assist a commander with planning are the commander's advisers.

clue.text: Also short of rum, et cetera

parts.note: and means also, in addition

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of short of are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone also seems to be running out of rum, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the old British adjective for odd, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Latin phrase and the English idiom mean and other things of the same kind.

clue.text: Witty remark about eastern passenger ship

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on art
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A clever quip is made concerning an oriental cruise vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A short joke or quip delivered in a single sentence is a witty remark.

clue.text: Work schedule in bistro, taxing

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A restaurant's staff timetable is demanding.
explanation.definitionFit: A list showing who works when is a duty schedule.

clue.text: Sweet and sour delivery

parts.note: acid means sour-tasting
a drop is a delivery, as in a parcel drop

explanation.surface: A shipment arrives that is both pleasant and unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart boiled sweet is a British confectionery, so it is a sweet in the sense of a candy.

clue.text: Challenged about feeding my old man

indicators.note: feeding means the word for about goes into the word for father

parts.note: my old man is slang for one's father, dad
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone was disputed over feeding their father.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare someone is to challenge them to do something risky.

clue.text: Walking aid, article found in church

indicators.note: found in means the article sits inside the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A walking stick has been discovered in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick used for support when walking is a walking aid.

clue.text: Unreasonableness shown by Irish supporter about quota

definitions.note: an adverb phrase: acting with unreasonableness on show

indicators.note: about means the Irish supporter goes round the quota

parts.note: an ally is a supporter
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: An Irish backer is unreasonable about the share they are allotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without reason or logic is behaving with unreasonableness on display.

clue.text: A ploy to detain Hamlet, initially for a brief period

indicators.note: to detain means the ploy word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a wile is a trick or ploy

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Hamlet

explanation.surface: A scheme to keep Hamlet in custody, at least for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means for a short time, so it can replace the phrase for a brief period.

clue.text: Silence head of administration, slightly crazy

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

indicators.note: head of means take the first letter of administration

explanation.surface: Muzzling the chief of an administration seems a little mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone senile or infatuated and not quite rational is described as crazy.

clue.text: Ready money in strong bag brought back by husband

parts.note: hard means strong or tough

indicators.note: brought back means the bag word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sac is a bag-like pouch

explanation.surface: Cash kept in a sturdy bag is returned by a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is coins and notes to hand, as opposed to cheques or credit.

clue.text: Spots some in open carriage heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards
some in means part of the letters is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Pimples are seen on someone in an open-topped carriage travelling north.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition causing pimples is described in short as spots.

clue.text: Willing to participate, worker readily available

parts.note: if you are on, you are game to join in
a hand is a manual worker

explanation.surface: An eager labourer is ready and waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearby and ready for use is idiomatically said to be at your disposal.

clue.text: Quickly getting in a large car

indicators.note: getting in means the next letters go inside the word for quickly

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long

explanation.surface: Someone climbs swiftly into a big car.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for a sedan, a car with a closed body and separate boot.

clue.text: Snakes, excellent specimens

definitions.meaning: an old informal word for a first-rate thing or person

explanation.surface: Fine examples of serpents.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, rattlesnakes go by this short name, and old slang uses it for anything first-rate.
